title: NFL Jersey Quiz: Hard Mode
headline: Can You Name The NFL Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Jersey?
description: A hard NFL jersey quiz: eight tiny squares cut from current NFL jerseys, no numbers, no wordmarks, no logos. Just a stripe, a collar or a shoulder. Guess the team, reveal the answer, keep score.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from a current NFL jersey, about one sixtieth of the whole picture. No numbers, no wordmarks, no logo patches. What is left is the stuff fans stop noticing: a sleeve stripe, a collar, a shoulder panel.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.piece: Orange and white stripes near the cuff of the navy home sleeve.
items.fact: The Bears wear the initials GSH on the left sleeve for founder George S. Halas, who died in 1983.

items.piece: Orange tiger stripes over the black shoulder.
items.fact: Cincinnati unveiled its current uniforms in 2021, with tiger stripes over the shoulders.

items.piece: Orange and white stripes at the end of the brown sleeve.
items.fact: The Browns are the only NFL team with no logo on the helmet: it is plain orange.

items.piece: Gold and white stripes on the green sleeve.
items.fact: Vince Lombardi made green and gold the Packers' permanent colors in 1959, his first season as coach.

items.piece: Two white stripes over the royal blue shoulder.
items.fact: The Colts brought their blue-and-white look and the horseshoe with them when they moved from Baltimore to Indianapolis in 1984.

items.piece: White and gold stripes on the red sleeve.
items.fact: The franchise began play as the Dallas Texans in 1960 and moved to Kansas City as the Chiefs in 1963.

items.piece: A navy point cutting into the orange sleeve.
items.fact: Denver introduced its current uniforms in 2024, its first full redesign since 1997.

items.piece: Silver and white stripes above the cuff of the blue sleeve.
items.fact: The Lions chose blue and silver in 1934, their first season in Detroit. The name Honolulu blue did not show up in print until 1948.
